g.title: GCMS_QC_Flow
g.text: GC-MS PETN/RDX Injection & Sample Acceptance Flowchart (Revised v3)
STATUS: TARGET DESIGN -- describes the INTENDED future pipeline. Sections A and D, and several
Section B/C refinements below, are NOT yet implemented in the live script (see legend notes).

g.title: cluster_A
g.text: SECTION A -- Blank Injection Evaluation (run for every blank)

g.title: cluster_B
g.text: SECTION B -- QC Evaluation (both PETN & RDX; each level bracketed pre- & post- sample block)

g.title: cluster_C
g.text: SECTION C -- Per-Analyte Evaluation (run INDEPENDENTLY for PETN and for RDX; NCs run the IDENTICAL tree EXCEPT at the 0.2ng bracket check -- see C_ROWTYPE, NOTE7)

g.title: cluster_D
g.text: SECTION D -- Combine Per-Analyte Results into ONE Row-Level Outcome (FIRST-FAILURE-ONLY policy, fixed check order: IS -> PETN -> RDX)

g.title: A_CONTAM
g.text: Flag as HIGH carryover-risk for any

g.title: A_OTHER
g.text: does NOT set a carryover-risk flag
(no PETN/RDX signal was seen, so there

g.title: BLANK_REG
g.text: flags a blank here -- a non-target peak (A_OTHER)
counts as CLEAN for this register.
Read by the bracketing-blank check in Section C.

g.title: B_HASMORE
g.text: Is a further QC of the SAME

g.title: QC_REG
g.text: QC Bracket Status Register (per analyte, per level)
Evaluated at BOTH the pre- and post- QC injection
0.2ng now stores TWO independent bracket verdicts per
analyte from the SAME injection -- DETECTABILITY (read
by Negative Control rows) and QUANTIFICATION (read by
real Sample rows); see Section C, C_ROWTYPE:
• Combined = PASS only if pre AND post are BOTH present
AND BOTH PASS (for whichever register applies)
• Combined = WARN only if BOTH present and at least one
is WARN (0.2ng only -- 6ng has no WARN tier)
• Combined = FAIL if EITHER side is MISSING (incl. an
injection failure with no usable substitute) or FAILED
-- both sides are REQUIRED, for either register

A ratio-based check was also rejected -- RDX's

g.title: KEY
g.text: Amber = WARN / qualitative flag / flagged design change
Purple hexagon = routing node (recalls an earlier

g.title: NOTE1
g.text: Every decision node shows BOTH outcomes

g.title: NOTE2
g.text: ANY detected peak, not only quantifiable ones --
a 'trace' result can also be carryover.

g.title: NOTE3
g.text: Bracket checks are now CONDITIONAL on tier, not
universal: 6ng (accuracy) is only checked when this
only checked when this analyte is Trace or Negative.
A missing pre- or post- QC counts as FAIL, not WARN
further from the sample block can be substituted for
an injection-failed bracket QC (Section B fallback).

g.title: NOTE3B
g.text: CONFIRMED DESIGN DECISION: there is NO override at
either bracket gate, for samples or NCs -- a missing/
failed bracket is always a hard FAIL, whichever
register it is checked against. UPDATED 2026-09-08:
the 6ng gate remains identical for samples and NCs
(one register, one check). The 0.2ng gate now checks
TWO different registers depending on row type (see
NOTE3C, NOTE7) -- Samples and NCs no longer necessarily
see the SAME verdict from the SAME underlying QC
injection at 0.2ng, even though neither ever gets an

g.title: NOTE3C
g.text: concentration can floor to exactly 0 even at good SNR --
the fitted calibration curve's own y-intercept (an
artefact of a weighted quadratic fit through a handful
of real standards, not a physical measurement) can sit
ABOVE a genuine low-level response, so no concentration
>=0 on that curve reproduces it. This is a curve-fitting
artefact, not evidence of a non-detect -- confirmed via
direct comparison against the raw response and against
calibration-floor case. DECISION: a Sample's own reported
recovery % still needs a real number, so Samples keep the
unchanged from the pre-2026-09-08 behaviour. A Negative
Control's contamination verdict only ever needs 'was
something detected', so NCs use the new DETECTABILITY
flag (SNR only) instead -- a real detection no longer
gets silently reclassified as 'Not evaluated' purely
because of where the calibration curve happens to

g.title: NOTE4
g.text: IS-ratio quantification for RDX only (15N-RDX is
not a valid drift proxy for PETN -- tested and
rejected); drift correction for PETN only;
sensitivity WARN tier is now identical for both

g.title: NOTE5
g.text: Row-level outcome (Section D) uses a FIXED,
agreed check order -- IS, then PETN, then RDX --
and reports ONLY the first blocking failure found.
The IS check short-circuits immediately at C1 (see
C_NOINJECT / C_ISLOW -- BOTH IS outcomes are hard
FAILs as of 2026-08-11) -- it does NOT wait for
Section D; only PETN-vs-RDX ordering is resolved
there, since IS already gates entry to the

g.title: NOTE6
g.text: trace-level detection is a genuine, reportable
outcome, not an automatic reanalysis trigger --
this is a deliberate departure from the current
today auto-FAILs ANY sample with a detected-but-
currently only a fully Quantifiable result or a
true no-peak-at-all (NA) avoids FAIL. Under this
chart, a Trace result ALWAYS carries a WARNING
caveat forward (Section D, D4) -- if every other
check passes, the row is PASS*, never a plain
PASS, reflecting the reduced confidence of an

g.title: NOTE7
g.text: run the IDENTICAL tree EXCEPT for exactly ONE point --
the 0.2ng bracket check (Section C, C_ROWTYPE/C7): a
Sample reads the QUANTIFICATION register, an NC reads
the DETECTABILITY register (Section B, NOTE3C). This is
a deliberate, narrow divergence, not a return to the old
asymmetric design -- both row types still go through the
bracket, and Section D combination logic; only WHICH
0.2ng verdict is consulted differs, and only because a
contamination check and a quantified-recovery check are
genuinely different questions with different evidence
requirements. NCs and samples otherwise still diverge
only in reporting-label vocabulary at the very end (e.g.

g.title: NOTE8
g.text: PETN's second monitored ion (m/z57) was tested and
REJECTED as a confirmatory requirement -- only 18.2%
of pure Cal standards ever reach a measurable SNR for
it, so requiring it would fail most genuine detections,
not catch misidentifications. m/z76 alone is used.
RDX requires BOTH its monitored ions (m/z46, m/z75) --
both are reliably detected (~100% in Cal standards) and
requiring both costs zero extra failures on any real
Sample/QC/Cal row in the study. A ratio-based check
and rejected: RDX's ratio showed real, significant
so a single fixed ratio+tolerance would not be valid
across the calibration range -- a qualitative detection
check (SNR ≥ 3) was used instead. A full-scan (m/z
41-200) survey at PETN's RT found no better second
qualifier candidate than the currently-monitored ions.

g.title: NOTE9
g.text: Reanalysis selection (NOT diagrammed above -- a separate
stage that runs AFTER this per-injection acceptance chart,
once multiple physical re-analyses of the same Sample/NC
exist): as of 2026-09-08, select_best_attempt() prefers the
B's B3/B_QUANT_PASS evidence) instead of the earliest date.
A Negative Control's own genuinely clean result (no peak on
EITHER analyte, i.e. both C_NEGATIVE) is trusted as the best
possible outcome outright, rather than an unranked unknown --
since a clean result and a small-but-nonzero 6ng bias are not
otherwise on a directly comparable numeric scale. NOT applied
to real Samples: a Sample's own no-peak result is not
obviously a BETTER outcome than a low-bias detection the way
a clean NC result is, so Samples still fall through to the
date-based tie-break unchanged. See ASTRA/doe/CONTEXT.md and
on Reanalysis" session, for full detail.
